correctness.rationale: Every generic section vertex corresponds to one crossed edge. The 8 algebraic vertex directions of the uniform square antiprism form a simple 8-great-circle arrangement with exactly 56 intersection vertices, 112 arcs and 58 regions; 58 explicitly feasible sign masks exhaust that bound. Exact Q[t]/(t^4-2) arithmetic yields precisely 24 six-crossing masks and 34 eight-crossing masks, and height rescaling preserves possible section types. Eight base and eight lateral edges have correlations s/(1+s) and (1/sqrt(2)-s)/(1+s), respectively. Opposite-sign Haar probabilities are arccos(correlation)/pi. Expectation yields the full two-point section spectrum; the derivative is positive for every s>0, and limits are 0 and 1. Independent numerical section hull checks and height samples agree. The proof excludes only measure-zero exceptional planes. Exact executable package paths are included as standalone files.

value.rationale: The right square antiprism is a standard natural polyhedron family. Its complete Haar central-section polygon-type spectrum is unexpectedly binary for every positive height, and the two-type structural fact combines with the edge-angle identity to provide an exact global one-parameter probability law. Strict monotonicity gives inverse determination of the aspect ratio from one scalar observable, including sharp endpoint limits and a closed nontrivial uniform-antiprism benchmark. This is a motivated complete natural-family classification rather than a tiny numerical improvement or arbitrary parameter slice.
